intentAndPurpose.intent: Trigger a single user action with clear emphasis and accessible states.

rules.name: bold
pairWith: secondary action as subtle or ghost

props.name: attention
props.description: Emphasis level — high (bold fill), medium (subtle/tinted fill), low (ghost, text-only). Drives the visual treatment; the component derives the internal variant + `data-variant` from this.

props.name: condensed
props.description: Condensed mode: reduces height and horizontal padding while keeping the same typography. Use for dense layouts, inline actions, and compact UI areas. NOT the same as using a smaller size. Only applies when `contained={true}`.

props.name: contained
props.description: Whether the button renders in its contained form (filled pill with a state-layer wrapper) or its uncontained form (transparent, underlined, text-link style). Mirrors the Figma `Contained` variant property on the Button component set. Props that only make sense for the contained form (`condensed`, `fullWidth`, `decoration`) are ignored when `contained={false}`.

props.name: decoration
props.description: Direct decoration config — overrides DecorationContext. Use in Storybook stories or tests where context may not propagate.

interactionBehavior.summary: Button responds on three channels at once: the fill steps to a hover/pressed token, the whole button scales DOWN slightly on press, and focus draws a two-layer halo that survives tinted surfaces. Press scale is size-aware — small buttons squash more than large ones, and full-width buttons barely move. `loading` implies disabled: the click handler stops firing, the label goes transparent but stays in the accessibility tree, and a centred spinner takes over without the button changing size.
hover: The fill steps to the hover token for the resolved attention level: `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` at `attention="high"`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` at `medium`, `--{Role}-Hover` at `low`.
Border colour, text colour, and the solid stroke colour each have their own hover channel, so a brand can recolour the outline on hover without touching the fill.
Wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover fill behind.
Never applies while `disabled` or `loading` — every hover rule is qualified with `:not(.disabled)`.

Buttons with a brand material (gradient) fill deliberately keep the fill stable on hover; the feedback comes from the tap-scale and decoration channels instead, because a flat colour swap over a gradient reads as a glitch.
press: The fill deepens to the pressed token — `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed`, or `--{Role}-Pressed` by attention level.
The entire button scales DOWN on press: `scale(1 - tapScale/100)`. Note this is opposite to Checkbox and Radio, whose state layers scale UP on press.

Tap scale is size-aware: 7% at size XS (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-XS`), 3% for S through XL (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`), and only 1% when `fullWidth` (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-FullWidth`) — a wide button moving 3% would read as the whole page shifting.
Press applies on touch as well as pointer; it is not `(hover: hover)`-guarded.
A brand can disable the squash entirely by setting the tap-scale token to 0, as Stepper does.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring in `--Focus-Outline`, so the indicator stays visible when the button sits inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
`:focus` alone clears the native outline — the visible indicator is `:focus-visible` only, so mouse clicks do not paint a ring.
Ring width and colour are brand-overridable via `--Button-focusOutlineWidth` and `--Button-focusOutlineColor`.

Ornament-decorated buttons cannot use a rectangular box-shadow ring, so they drop the box-shadow and dilate their own masked silhouette with an SVG `feMorphology` filter (`#oneui-btn-focus-ring`) — the halo then follows the pointed caps exactly instead of boxing them.
Decorated ghost buttons instead recolour their decoration strokes to the focus colour, since there is no fill to ring.
keyboard: Renders a native `<button>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both activate it with no custom key handling — and `Space` fires on key-up, `Enter` on key-down, per platform convention.
`type` defaults to the native `submit` behaviour inside a form unless you pass `type="button"` — a common source of accidental form submits.
Disabled and loading buttons are removed from the tab order because the native `disabled` attribute is applied (not `aria-disabled`).
loading: `loading` implies disabled — internally `isDisabled = disabled || loading` — so the native `disabled` attribute is set and `onClick` / `onPress` stops firing. You do not need to pass both.
`aria-busy="true"` is set so assistive tech announces the pending state.

The start slot, label, and end slot go to `opacity: 0` rather than `display: none`, which keeps their boxes in layout — the button does not resize or reflow when loading toggles — and keeps the label in the accessibility tree so the button still has a name.
The spinner is absolutely positioned across the button's box, so it lands centred over the hidden content regardless of label length.
`pointer-events: none` is applied, so hover and press visuals are inert while loading.
disabled: Dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` (brand-overridable via `--Button-disabledOpacity`) and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`.

Because `pointer-events: none` is set on a natively disabled button, the `not-allowed` cursor is not actually observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. This is a known, accepted system-wide gap; do NOT wrap the button in a host element to work around it (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
All hover and press rules are suppressed via `:not(.disabled)`, so a disabled button is visually inert.
touch: Hover fills never apply on touch-only devices; the pressed fill plus the tap-scale squash are the entire response to a tap.
Size XS carries the largest tap scale (7%) precisely because it is the hardest target to confirm visually at a glance on a phone.
